title: Police need details of mental patients before apprehension: coroner's jury
article: Police should be given details of the history of mental patients before apprehending them in distraught situations, a coroner's jury in Vernon said Friday.
The jury made seven recommendations following an inquest into the death of Christopher Paul Klim, 24, who was first jolted by a Taser and then shot dead in December last year.

Police entered Klim's apartment to arrest him on a mental health warrant obtained under the Canadian Mental Health Act. Klim, who had schizophrenia, was holding a knife in his left hand, the inquest heard.

Officers attempted to subdue Klim with a Taser when he refused to put down the knife, the inquest heard, but he didn't calm down. Two officers testified they felt their lives were endangered when Klim lunged at them with the knife. As a result, they shot him twice, and the second bullet killed him, the inquest heard.
The coroner's jury recommended Friday that mental health warrants forwarded to police should contain details of the patients' mental illness history, behaviours and potential response to authority.
It also recommended the ministry of health and provincial health regions develop a provincial policy on the apprehension of mental patients when police assistance is required.
Another recommendation made to the solicitor general is that police receive more training in managing mental health patients.
James Cotter, the lawyer for Klim's family, said they are satisfied with the recommendations and hope police will adopt them and handle people with mental illness better in future.
